omitted_concepts.description: James Robinson (University of Chicago) and his work "The Narrow Corridor" exploring how societies balance state and social power, noted as more ethnographically informed than Acemoglu.

Abhijit Banerjee & Esther Duflo (MIT), development economists who spend time on the ground, Nobel winners who listen to people they study, and their book "Good Economics for Hard Times" incorporating cultural and social factors.

Post-Keynesian Economics: Steve Keen (incorporates network effects, critiques mathematical formalism) and Stephanie Kelton (Modern Monetary Theory, emphasizes political/social factors shaping policy).

Ecological Economics: Herman Daly studies economy as embedded in social and ecological systems, emphasizes cultural values and social cooperation, "Beyond Growth" integrates social and environmental factors.

Economic Sociologists: Mark Granovetter (pioneer of embeddedness theory, informal networks drive outcomes), Viviana Zelizer (cultural meanings shape economic behavior), Richard Swedberg (entrepreneurship from social networks).
Latin American Structuralism: Fernando Fajnzylber (ECLAC tradition) emphasizes cultural/institutional factors in development and network-based industrial development.
Chinese Institutional Economics: Justin Yifu Lin studies informal institutions guiding China's development, "Demystifying the Chinese Economy" shows cultural adaptation of markets.
African Development Economics: Benno Ndulu studies traditional institutions interacting with modern markets, emphasizes social networks and cultural practices.
Digital Economics: Shoshana Zuboff studies surveillance capitalism, technology shaping social behavior, combines economics with cultural analysis of digital transformation.
Platform Economics: Nick Srnicek studies platform capitalism, digital networks reshaping economics, Marxist-influenced but empirically grounded.

review.summary: All 25 claims are supported by the cited passages. The claims accurately capture the source's description of a marginalized 'messy life' economist ecosystem, their methodological strengths for AI prediction, institutional challenges, and specific contributions of 8 named economists. The extraction omits 10 other significant economist groups and individuals detailed in the source, including James Robinson, Banerjee & Duflo, Post-Keynesian and Ecological schools, economic sociologists, regional traditions (Latin American, Chinese, African), and contemporary digital/platform economists.
